newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet seeks N.Y. route, eases booking.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet seeks N.Y. route, eases booking.

text.p: Travel agents will soon be able to book flights on ValuJet Airlines by computer and the low-fare carrier has asked for permission to resume serving New York City, officials said Wednesday.

The company also said it was implementing a programme to install smoke detectors in all of its airplane cargo holds, a measure urged by federal transportation officials after the crash of ValuJet Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades last May.

The airline said it has asked the Department of Transportation for special clearance to serve New York City's LaGuardia Airport from its Atlanta base because Delta Air Lines' dominance has led to high fares on the route.

"We remain extremely optimistic that there will be some access made to LaGuardia for ValuJet," Ponder Harrison, senior vice president for sales and marketing, told Reuters. "Prices are extremely high. They are almost 300 percent higher than when ValuJet served that market a year ago."
ValuJet briefly operated flights to LaGuardia in the spring of 1996. Harrison said the company would want enough slots "to have a meaningful schedule. We flew five flights daily a year ago."

Travel agents will soon be able to book flights on ValuJet through computer reservation systems, instead of having to call the airline's reservation agents, ValuJet President D. Joseph Corr told an annual shareholders meeting.

"We are going to join the computerized reservation system. It will start in early June ... By the end of June we will be in full-time," Corr said. "Clearly, we have to come up with more ways to distribute our product. The formula that we had before is not sufficient by itself."

ValuJet said it has already begun testing a prototype system for putting smoke detectors in all of its airplane cargo holds. James Jense, senior vice president of maintenance and engineering, said a test system has produced "excellent results" and that ValuJet hoped the Federal Aviation Administration would approve it soon.
Federal aviation officials have urged the installation of smoke detectors and fire suppressors in all passenger airline cargo holds because of last May's ValuJet crash.
"As soon as we have approval, we'll begin to put them in," Jensen said. "Within approximately 15 months, we'll have our fleet completely done."

The company said it had $138.8 million in cash on hand at the end of March 1997. "In the next 60 fays, we expect a cash refund from the Internal Revenue Service for an additional $35 million," Corr said.

He said the airline has no specific merger plans. "I think everybody in the low-fare industry is talking to one another," Corr said. "We have had a lot of discussions. At this time we have nothing to report on whether we ever get a deal or not."
